newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Grolsch prunes German beer operations.
newsitem.headline: Grolsch prunes German beer operations.

text.p: Dutch brewer Grolsch has pruned its activities in Germany, where it has a distribution and promotion agreement with Brau und Brunnen AG, newspaper Het Financieele Dagblad said on Saturday.

The paper said both brewers denied the cut back was in response to falling sales but under the two-year old agreement between the two firms distribution of Grolsch pilsner will be limited to Berlin, Hamburg and North Rhine Westfalia.
Brau und Brunnen said it was limiting sales of Grolsch becasuse it was only popular in bigger cities, where it is seen as a speciality beer, Het Financieele Dagblad said.

In December Brau und Brunnen announced it would rationalise it operations, shedding capcity and streamline its portfolio of beer brands in a bid to return to profit by 1998. The group said it would make unspecified losses in 1996 and 1997.
